items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: And while he's blowin', Hawk walks in, Coleman Hawkins, and he start to blowin'.

ctx.x: On 133rd Street, a little joint down there called Mexico's. Let me see... This little room in here would be about the size of the place -- a little-bitty room. Greely was blowin' when I walked in, which I didn't know Greely, but... Boy, I was amazed. The place was full of musicians, and he's blowin'... Hey, I never heard no saxophone like that. I'm telling you.

And while he's blowin', Hawk walks in, Coleman Hawkins, and he start to blowin'. Well, he was the master, you know. Well, there was something different when he blowed, too. Nobody else would play no more tenor. They wouldn't play it. Couldn't get 'em to play it.
